I thought he lost pretty clearly to Holloway and Jean Silva, but he had great moments in the striking against both guys, and they are elite strikers. The Evloev one was so close that I think I initially scored it for Allen. Costa is a real talent, but Allen is durable as hell. He's not going to get head kick TKO'd like Charriere or Dan Ige. And Costa has showed cardio issues in that fight with Erosa. I reckon that Allen maintains the pace, and we either see him win a decision, or we get the ultra-rare Arnold Allen finish.

Choi vs. Santos
Daniel Santos, TKO, R2
Banger fight. I like both dudes, but Choi lost some great years of his career to the mandatory military service, and I think Daniel Santos is really that dude at 145. Maybe Santos never makes it into the rankings, but the way he slimed out Castaneda and Joo Sang Yoo was super impressive to me. Choi isn't a slouch himself, so this fight is pretty close, but Santos is younger, and I think he has more power and more of a chance to land big, damaging shots if this turns into a firefight.

Wellmaker vs. Díaz
Malcolm Wellmaker, TKO, R1
Juan Diaz seems like a decent prospect, but I think people are hopping off the Wellmaker train too early. Ethyn Ewing looks like he's going to be a title contender or at the very least a top 10 fighter, and Wellmaker had some strong moments against him. I realize that Ewing pulled up on like six minutes' notice and showed Wellmaker levels, but Wellmaker still looked like he belonged in that fight, and he did a helluva lot better than Estevam. If this makes it out of the first round, Wellmaker is going to start to fade, and I could see Diaz taking rounds two and three, but I think the safer play here is Wellmaker by early TKO or 29-28 DEC.

Bukauskas vs. Bellato
Modestas Bukauskas, DEC
Coin flip fight here. Bukauskas looked pretty shoddy against old Krylov, and Bellato had a career-best performance against Luke Fernandez, plus he didn't look all that bad against Navajo Stirling. I don't like that Modestas is training out of his garage or whatever because apparently Tom Aspinall's gym has completely shut down, and none of Modestas's wins are too impressive. Still, I think he shows better technique than Bellato, even if there's less raw power. Might switch.

Cuamba vs. Sopaj
Benardo Sopaj, DEC
Pretty close fight against two young prospects. These guys both seem to have pretty well-developed skillsets despite their spotty records. Cuamba took his debut on short notice against Oki up at 155, which is really not his proper weight class. Sopaj, meanwhile, took the first two rounds off of Vinicius Oliveira before gassing and getting knocked tf out by a flying knee. And that was on his debut. Beating Ricky Turcios doesn't mean all that much, but based on the Vinicius performance, I think I have to go with Sopaj here.

Veretennikov vs. Williams
Khaos Williams, TKO, R1
Hard one to pick. Khaos Williams has the more impressive wins in the UFC, but Veretennikov is actually a pretty decent striker when he's not getting taken down, and I don't think that Williams will shoot all that much. I might switch this one, but my early lean is Khaos because I think he has more power and more of a danger factor. Veretennikov has horrible moments in every fight he's in. I have trouble picking Khaos because I know he's a real estate developer and only does MMA as a side hustle, but he's younger, stronger, and more dangerous. Might switch.

Tokkos vs. Erslan
Ivan Erslan, DEC
Dear lord. How am I supposed to pick this? I mean, Erslan's grappling defense looked woeful against Jimmy Crute, but he put on a better show in that Cutelaba fight. I don't know, Tokkos only got that one win in the UFC because he was fighting a Tafa with zero grappling.

Gantt vs. Ogden
Tommy Gantt, SUB, R2
I don't know, Ogden seems to just give up when the going gets tough, and at 36 years old, I don't favor him fighting against a powerful debuting guy, even if the debuting guy is 33 himself. I reckon Erslan's grappling defense will be good enough to withstand Tokkos. Might switch.

Vieira vs. Cavalcanti
Jacqueline Cavalcanti, DEC
Bruh idk

Bannon vs. Caliari
Nicolle Caliari, DEC
Shauna Bannon is the better striker I guess, but Caliari is the much better wrestler. Bannon looks lost whenever the fight hits the mat despite the fact that she's supposedly a BJJ black belt I think. I don't feel strongly either way on this feet, but

Brundage vs. Petroski
Petroski, DEC
I think that Brundage has a very good chance of knocking Petroski tf out with a left or right hook, but I don't like the idea of picking Brundage. Of course Brundage should be able to win if he sticks to a decent gameplan, but how can I trust Brundage to ever stick to a gameplan? He doesn't even listen to his corner, and even in favorable matchups that Brundage should win (like McConico or SD Dumas), he finds a way to lose. He's got a decent chance here, but I feel like I can't pick him.

Barez vs. Gurule
Gurule, DEC
Can't believe I'm picking Luis Gurule to win a UFC fight, but Barez hasn't looked great himself, and dude is 37 years old at flyweight with some significant cardio issues once the fight makes it into R2 or R3. Gurule by split decision. Might switch.

Ardelean vs. Viana
Ardelean, DEC
Bruh idk

Tokkos vs Erslan
Erslan KO RD 2

Gotta be a loser goes home bout here; it goes without saying if Erslan loses but I assume this is the last fight on Tokkos’s contract as well. I understand why most of Tap is on Tokkos but I can’t back him here; he is like Brundage, one of those guys who you never have a good reason to back. He trains and coaches a lot of elite guys at Kill Cliff but none of that has rubbed off on him. He is average everywhere, has no cardio, and hates getting hit. His last fight was the first time he’s ever showed any form of grit but I think it really speaks to how bad of a grappler Tafa is; even then he still had Tokkos looking for the door in r2 but his grappling is just so piss poor that it backfired. In every other fight Tokkos has 3 minutes of fight in him before he starts playing defense. Not just in the UFC either, his regional tape is the exact same. Erslan was always a very questionable signing to me, so I'm not really surprised he’s lost every fight he’s had; at least Tokkos was short notice, Erslan never should’ve been called up. He couldn’t even have a winning record in KSW and his game is pretty limited. That being said, I still think he’s a better fighter than Tokkos. These guys are both regional quality fighters, but to back Tokkos I feel like you are just relying on his opponent to quit. That could happen, as Erslan’s last fight was straight up pathetic but for all his flaws, Crute is still a very good grappler when he gets on top. I don’t think it will be easy for Tokkos to recreate that, nor is his grappling anywhere as good. Tokkos is going to grapple here like always, I expect Erslan to get taken down as everyone in the UFC has done to him. However, he’s actually not that easy to hold down. He was able to hit reversals on both Crute and Ion (he actually managed to outwrestle Ion weirdly enough), and while taken down by Navajo he didn’t let him do much with it. Seeing these fights is enough for me to trust Erslan, I think Tokkos is an extremely low level grappler and all you really need is basic understanding to survive and defend. I am not remotely impressed with Erslan but his grappling is not as bad as it seems. I don’t think it will be as easy as last fight for Tokkos, and he will give up under any form of resistance. If Tokkos can’t get takedowns, I think he is going to resign to losing. He hates getting hit, has a bad chin, and can’t strike at all. Once he tires he just runs away and looks to get the fight down as soon as possible. Erslan is a pretty low level striker but he has power and at least goes for it. Tokkos hasn’t ko’ed anyone with a pulse in his entire career and has looked harmless in any of his fights outside the regional scene. His body language and heart is godawful, all Erslan needs to do is walk him down and throw, and Tokkos will be looking for the door. Erslan is really low iq so I kind of expect him to drag this on, but once Tokkos gasses this is Erslan’s fight to lose. I don’t even think he’s that much better than Tokkos, but he simply makes an effort to win past 5 minutes. I think Tokkos got really lucky that Tafa has no grappling, every other fight of his he usually gives up when he can’t get takedowns. Erslan isn’t some cardio machine but I haven’t really seen him gas out, so all he needs to do is not give up takedowns and he should be able to beat Tokkos. I think he can get a KO but I’m also expecting him to make this harder than it needs to be.

Ogden vs Gantt
Gantt SUB RD 1

Finally a good fight, I’ve been patiently waiting for Gantt’s debut; I think he’s got a lot of potential. I don’t like his age because it limits his ceiling, but he’s clearly in his physical prime and I think his skillset is pretty nuts. Gantt is a bit of a mystery given his age and level of comp but he looks like the goods if im being completely honest. His wrestling has perfectly translated to MMA, hes a phenomenal athlete, his striking needs work but is surprisingly good for a lifetime wrestler with no experience, and he’s shown good cardio. He has faced anyone good (even on dwcs) but Gantt is handling all of them like he should be; the only time ive seen him struggle was the paulson fight where he got dropped. However, he did recover well and it is worth noting that he fought at 185 there, those things happen when you’re in the wrong weight class. Gantt also switched camps to DC's new gym full time. I think very highly of DC’s camp in general but I think DC is a perfect coach for a wrestler like Gantt; Gantt has already adapted his wrestling flawlessly (imo) and has the tools to be a really good fighter despite his age/inexperience. This is a great debut for him because Ogden is a weasel, but also one I expect him to dominate in. Ogden is the definition of an overachiever, he’s very mediocre and has no athletic talents but he’s been able to win fights because he gameplans well and is good at targeting weak points. I think his skillset is below average and he’s just a regular joe for the most part. He has decent grappling and serviceable enough striking, but anyone better in those areas can easily outwork him. I think this is honestly the perfect debut for Gantt because Ogden has absolutely no threat of chinning him and is a grappler who is bad off of his back. Ogden does have good fundamentals and I definitely think he’s a better striker than Gantt, but he doesn’t do anything to get Gantt’s respect on the feet. He fights very passive and technical, but that will work against him since Gantt is going to look to wrestle. Even then, for being a wrestler Gantt’s striking is not bad at all. Usually wrestlers only have an overhand and look clunky but he strikes like someone who’s been doing it for a while; given his natural athletic talent and his career progression I assume he is someone who picks things up very quickly (also another reason I like him training with DC so much). Ogden has a 100% tdd on paper but against who? He still finds ways to lose minutes on his back, Moises and Leavitt were able to outgrapple him without scoring a single takedown; pretty awful look honestly. Even his last win against Loik was a bad look; for starters he clearly lost r2/3 on damage, so this was a trash decision. He was taking Loik down at will but Loik reversed him in r2/3 and easily put the damage on. Ogden wins these fights with lay n pray, he’s not even a dangerous grappler. Gantt has yet to prove himself but I feel very confident that Ogden is not outwrestling him. Gantt is a far superior athlete and he was a legit wrestler before MMA (ACC champion at NC State), his wrestling has quite frankly looked elite on tape; I know he’s fought nobodies but you can clearly see the skill level in the things he does. Ogden is not a good wrestler at all IMO, and I don’t see him being able to top time Gantt. I think Gantt is gonna take him down early and show levels. Ogden is a decent black belt but I kind of think Gantt can bully his way into something like he did on dwcs. Ogden looks for the door when things get tough and he is outmatched here in just about every category. Gantt is a very legit prospect imo, I don’t know his ceiling but considering Grant Dawson reached top 15 with only wrestling, I think Gantt could replicate his success. He’s already more well rounded than him and I love his wrestling.

Viera vs Cavalcanti
Cavalcanti DEC

The UFC is really trying to shake up 135 with all of these bookings lately; they’re pushing out all the old guard. This dynamic feels very similar to what we saw a few weeks ago with Dumont/Edwards: You have a perennial top contender in Viera who is on a decline and fights close with everyone, versus a good prospect who’s been on a roll lately. I’ve always liked Cavalcanti. Her style can be a bit boring since she is a point fighter but I think she’s got great skills and fought pretty high competition as well. She beat Croden and Cornolle outside the ufc and has championship experience. I thought her only loss was a robbery, but it speaks to her fighting to her level of competition. She’s had two very clear wins in the ufc that were somehow splits because of this exact thing. Viera has been in the top 5 forever but I’ve never really been impressed with her; she also fights to her level of competition but also has a lot of bad habits that cost her fights. The worst example of this is the Yana fight, where she had like 12/13 minutes of control but absolutely 0 damage. She also dropped the ball in her last one because she was too focused on grappling. She fought a smart gameplan but didn’t think to mix in strikes and ultimately lost the fight, showing that she has not learned from the Yana fight. I am skeptical to back Cavalcanti since Viera is a really good grappler and Cavalcanti’s tdd is relatively untested. I think it is pretty good but she hasn’t faced many attempts nor someone on this level. I don’t think Viera is an amazing wrestler but she is strong and has good bjj so she could cause problems if she can get the fight down. I really didn’t like to see Cornolle/Avila hold her down though; Cavalcanti was never in danger and got to her feet easily, but neither of these girls are good grapplers so it’s not a great look. On the feet it will be really close, especially since this is the first quality striker Cavalcanti has faced in the ufc. However, Cavalcanti has very good technical ability and as mentioned Viera has awful habits that always cost her. She is extremely low volume and prefers control over damage. This could be how she wins but it could also be exactly how she loses this fight. Viera has only lost to the elite of the division the last few years but I do think she’s on a decline. Her wins are mostly unimpressive and with how the UFC has been booking the division recently, I’m pretty sure they are trying to get rid of her. Not confident in this one but I guess I’ll back Cavalcanti; I don’t really like picking Viera.

Petroski vs Brundage
Petroski DEC

Why is this even a fight? This legitimately could be the worst fight of the year contender if Petroski doesn’t get a finish. I decided after the MAM fight that I’m never going to tape Brundage again, if he doesn’t want to put effort into fighting then I’m not going to waste my time watching his fights either. There is never a good argument to pick Brundage imo, no matter what the odds are. The only time I ever picked him was when he fought Zach Reese, and even then I still feel like I got extremely lucky to get that pick right. Brundage’s win’s are all complete memes where he’s usually having to pull a win out of his ass. All his losses he makes a competitive effort for about 3-4 minutes and then takes the door the second it’s offered. This is actually a weird one because I rate Petroski at a similar level to Brundage lol. He definitely is a step above Brundage in terms of skills, but he has no good wins (I guess Viera), has never evolved since his debut, and has one foot out the door. He’s also lowkey just as much of a flake as Brundage; the Malkoun and Rowston fights being two pathetic quit jobs. Petroski is a better grappler than Brundage but his grappling is overrated as ****. All he does is lay n pray, it’s a miracle he has any subs because he never looks to advance position these days; probably because he’s scared of gassing. It’s lowkey scary backing him here because while fresh I can definitely see Brundage cracking him on the feet. I will never make a case to pick Brundage but r1 will be a sweat because he at least makes somewhat of a competitive effort; while fresh he’s 100% a better striker than Petroski and could make it hard to score takedowns. We did see him wobble Rowston very badly with a hook last fight, if he lands that on Petroski it’s almost a guarantee he takes the door. That being said though, I am not going to pick Brundage to win another UFC fight. I want to say Petroski finishes him, but that’s mostly cope because I am dreading watching 15 minutes of this; realistically I think this is a repeat of the Fremd fight. I think he’s just gonna spam takedowns and get 10-12 minutes of control while Brundage looks dejected and does **** all. If he loses this can we PLEASE cut Brundage? He is an embarrassment to the sport and not even entertaining 80% of the time.

Ardelean vs Viana Viana KO RD 2
This fight is somehow even lower level than Bannon/Caliari, I’m at least hoping it can be fun since Ardelean is scrappy and Viana (somehow) has a 100% finish rate, but my expectations are very low. It’s also wild to me how Ardelean has somehow won fights and still is fighting the bottom feeders of 115. Viana was always a fraud and I think her social media presence is the only reason she’s stayed around as long as she has. These girls are honestly on the same skill level, obviously they have different skillsets but they both have terrible records/losses and can only beat the worst of the worst in the ufc. I’ve never picked Viana to win a ufc fight but I think she has what it takes to compete here; I get why Ardelean is the favorite but that seems kind of disgusting to me. Sure, she is in better form but she’s fought four of the absolute worst fighters on the roster, lost a decision to Shauna Bannon, and robbed Melly of a KO (still somehow lost that fight). Viana has really bad losses herself but I think it should be around even; Ardelean being a favorite over someone with UFC wins is wrong. She may have overperformed but she is not magically a good fighter now. I also don’t really think Ardelean has the skillset to give Viana problems. On the feet she is scrappy, but idk how much success she will have here. She is at a huge size discrepancy, and Viana carries a ton of power for a 115er. Ardelean is not some master technician either and takes one to give one; like I said, this is a girl who managed to get outpointed by Melly and Bannon. Viana has at least competed on the feet against girls much better than Ardelean, which is enough for me to back her. The one thing that does really worry me is her output, since Ardelean has newfound confidence, but again I’m not sure she can be as aggressive as before since she’s fighting a girl with a big size advantage and power. The main path to victory everyone takes against Viana is takedowns. She has no tdd whatsoever and no urgency to get up either. She sits in guard and waits for an armbar, or gets submitted. Ardelean has gone for takedowns in every fight, and it’s very hard to back Viana knowing how bad her get ups are, but weirdly enough I don’t think Alice has much success here. She had a similar PTV in her last fight against a much worse girl and couldn’t do ****. She went 1/3 on takedowns and onyl scored 11 seconds of control on the one she did get. This goes without saying but she’s also not even close to the level of the girls that have been subbing Viana lately. Her habits on the ground are really bad but I also think she can get up here. Ardelean has poor control and isn’t some skilled grappler either. Viana was able to grapple with Lucindo early and got up a bunch against Ricci so that tells me she should be anle to stand up here; Ardelean is a massive step down from who she’s been fighting. I could also see a Viana sub frmo guard too. She has a 100% finish rate and the armbar is her signature submission. Ardelean is on the level of girls who she’s subbed in the past and I don’t think she has the grappling acumen to stay safe. I want to take Viana by decision but she’s never won a decision in her career so it’s strange. I don’t think Alice is going to wrestle that heavily and in that case I don’t know if a KO is that live. However, this is the same girl who got ko’ed by a body shot to Melly, so I suppose a KO is possible. This is a weird fight but I think Viana wins this one. Not sold on Ardelean at all for beating up on jobbers.

Barez vs Gurule
Barez KO RD 2

Glad to see Barez back, I’ve always really liked his game. He got to the UFC too late (should’ve been signed off of DWCS - great fight and I thought he won) but he has great skills and is usually finish or be finished. There definitely are a few red flags on his side such as age, really bad bottom game, 13 month layoff, and the beatdown he took last fight but skills wise this is an easy fight for him. Gurule is not UFC level. He’s not a bad fighter per se but he’s not good enough in any one category to win fights at the UFC level. His career has already been a disaster but he’s had three varying levels of opponents and fumbled in all of them. The Aguilar one is the one that told me he’s just not going to win any fights; losing to him is bad enough but losing a decision is irredeemable. Gurule was doing well filling the space but he lost that fight because every time Aguilar threw strikes he landed at will, and they had a much bigger effect than anything he was throwing. Gurule is my favorite term, a nothingburger. He just exists in the cage and doesn’t do anything to actively win the fight. He has no power, no real process, and a very wide stance that leaves him extremely open to being hit; as well as no head movement to compliment. He looks the part on the feet with his stance switches and feints but it’s all smoke and mirrors. Barez has a simple process on the feet but he throws everything straight down the middle and hits very hard for a 125er. I’ve always liked his boxing but he’s got good kicks as well; he was ******* Filho up with his body kicks before he got taken down. I think he should be able to land on Gurule at will here, he is going to stand in kicking range of Barez the entire fight and doesn’t actively look to shoot, so this should be Barez’s fight to lose. Barez has good enough grappling but he is terrible once grounded; he doesn’t know how to get up and has been subbed in most of his losses. This is a worry against capable guys but even if Gurule somehow does get him down, he doesn’t do anything with control. He was able to ground Ode for two minutes, which tells me he will wrestle when his opponents have a weakness to it, but the problem here is Barez has very good tdd. He does have a glaring weakness on the mat but getting him there is not super easy. It took Lima a 14 minute beatdown to find a sub and Filho nearly got ko’ed multiple times and needed 3 minutes of aggressive chain wrestling to get him down. Gurule just simply doesn’t do enough in the cage to chase a finish or actively outwrestle Barez IMO. Barez’s age and layoff does worry me a little, but he’s not facing a young prospect nor someone dangerous. I think he can probably KO Gurule too; he’s already proven his skills are not UFC level and now he’s facing a very dangerous striker who is hard to take down.

Bannon vs Caliari
Caliari SUB RD 1

This fight as a whole is just a complete meme. Loser goes home, unranked wmma against two really bad girls. Bannon never made sense as a signing to begin with, and Caliari is a flop from dwcs. I think Caliari is really bad but I actually like this matchup for her; she was getting screwed with the Foro fight but this is an extremely winnable matchup. Bannon (somehow) has UFC wins and a decent enough record but she is not a real fighter to me. She is competing at the lowest level possible and barely scraping by wins. Her “world champion kickboxing” background is fraudulent and her grappling is not even regional level. I believe she’s a blue/purple belt but her skills are white belt level; besides that meme armbar against Tomar, Bannon has easily been outgrappled in all of her UFC fights and once put on her back she has nothing. Hughes is very solid fighter but she absolutely dominated Bannon on the mat. Bannon is also an OF girl and does more posting in bikinis than she does training photos. Caliari is very bad herself but she at least has some skills; low level but at least she can do something. She’s had a really bad ufc run but this is a massive step down in comp. She’s also moving down to 115 which should help; she was way too small for 125 and while she had the physicality, it wasn’t enough. She also fought two of the biggest girls in the weight class which didn’t help. Caliari is pretty muscular so I think her physicality should translate pretty well here. Bannon somehow has the larger frame but Caliari is going to be bigger and stronger. The reason I like Caliari here is twofold: she grapples in every single one of her fights, and she has finishing ability. Grappling is the easiest way to beat Bannon, and I can rely on Caliari to force it here as she has done so in every fight in UFC/DWCS. Her wrestling is not good but you have to remember she faced two girls with really good tdd and massive frames; she was ragdolling Laframboise with some pretty nice throws in the clinch. Her control is not good but I don’t think that matters against Bannon since her grappling is legitimately terrible. Caliari’s TDA is bad but she has attempted 25 takedowns in a 3 fight sample size which is more than enough to tell me she can score them on Bannon; she can’t stop a chain wrestling attack and has bad enough tdd as it is. I think Caliari will probably submit her. She is an armbar merchant but again, that’s more than enough to finish Bannon I think. She doesn’t know what to do besides the wmma special armbar from guard, so Caliari could probably pass and even take the back if she wants. Even if she somehow gets reversed I actually do like her armbar; the one she hit on DWCS was pretty crafty, and even though a fraud that girl was like a 2nd degree black belt. I expect her to have better control at 115 though, she should be much more physical than Bannon. I would be shocked but if she chooses to strike she should win easily too. I don’t like her striking but she at least goes for it and has power; Bannon is a literal cardio kickboxer, all she does is circle the cage spamming her side kick to the body. Caliari just flails her arms around and does a lot of air punching, but she is at least aggressive which helps. I really don’t think Bannon can beat many people in striking at the ufc level, I mean she was literally seconds away from a KO loss to Puja Tomar of all people. This is a fight between two very low level girls fighting for their jobs, but as I always say, there are levels between a bad ufc fighter and someone who simply doesn’t belong.

Allen vs Costa
Allen DEC

I don’t feel like taping this one ; I pushed tape study too far and am burnt out from successive research. I have a terrible track record with Melky anyways so it’s probably not worth hearing my opinion regardless. His win streak has been impressive but I feel like he has highrolled a lot of his success with timing; a lot of these guys he’s beating are washed up vets. Being the first to ko Ige/Morgan was insanely impressive but at the end of the day both are journeymen with multiple losses; great fighters but they are not ranked level, I think especially so with Ige these days. Allen seems to always perform well in losses but always just comes up short; that being said, I think those three would wipe the floor with Melky if they fought. Allen seems like he’s on a decline on paper but he still seems pretty good. I honestly thought Silva was going to finish him but Allen looked pretty good considering the layoff. Both these guys are going to brawl with each other. Melky has a more diverse skillset on the feet but I really hate his boxing defense. I doubt Allen is the one to do it but he hits really hard and is easily the best boxer Costa has fought thus far. I also trust Allen to take over if this gets extended; I don’t think Costa has amazing cardio and his activity is going to take it’s toll at some point. You are bound to pick up some sort of injuries when you fight that much. His last two have been quick but I’ve seen Costa’s training footage before and he hard spars Joanderson Brito, old school Chute Boxe style with no headgear. He is more than prepared for a war but this training also kills your longevity and ensures you will get CTE post fighting career. I don’t have much of a technical read on this fight since I didn’t tape it; just going with Allen as a levels fight. This line seems wide as **** though, I don’t feel good fading Costa at dog odds again.

Choi vs Santos
Choi DEC

This isn’t as high stakes as the main event but I could lowkey see this fight stealing the show. These guys are never in boring fights and Santos is continuing his trend of fighting Korean brawlers; the prior two outings being really entertaining striking affairs. This is a really difficult fight to call: I was on Santos pre tape, started to like him a lot after seeing Choi’s recent fights, but then after seeing Santos’s win streak I’m kind of leaning back in the direction of Choi. Choi has looked amazing recently (also got robbed badly of a win against Nelson due to criminal refereeing from Tognoni) but is clearly showing some signs of regression. His wins are also aging like ****, Landwehr is finished, Nelson on the way out, and Algeo retiring after their fight. Willycat has been beating marginally better guys but imo his win streak hasn’t been that impressive either. At 145 he fought two inexperienced guys, and both of whom I thought were good matchups for him. I had an image in my head that he looked flawless at 145, but that’s not really the case. He has dealt with the size discrepancy well but he is very much a fat BW and it shows. He has to get in the pocket to work or else he punches at air and gets hit a ton. He does hit hard but I don’t think his power has translated super well; I think his recent fights have also inflated his power at this weight class because both his opponents had bad defense issues. Choi usually has sharp defense but it does falter in crazy fights (hence why he lost 3 in a row), so this is a worry. However, he did show much better resolve in the fight with Algeo. I think Choi is a lot more skilled than Santos, my worry with him is that he does fall apart a little bit. I think Willycat is going to have a lot of trouble with size here; he’s already really small for this weight class but Choi is a big FW. Choi knows how to fight behind range and he has shown some improvements on his time off; I do think he’s declined a bit physically but his grappling has improved a ton and his striking looked crisp against Algeo. Choi doesn’t react the best when hit and his defense does get lackadasical in brawls, but Willycat is super hittable himself. He is a classic Chute Boxe guy where he’s crazy durable and relies on his defense, but he eats punches on the chin frequently and even more so at 145. He was able to outvolume and pace Lee but throughout the fight Lee constantly clipped him on the chin. He also lost r1 to Yoo pretty clearly before the stoppage imo. I think Willycat is a tough fight but he’s also really beatable; he just breaks you with his pace. He does have good cardio but the ending of the Lee fight was a little concerning imo; Lee was exhausted so he pulled through but Willycat was slowing down a lot himself. He’s also really out of shape and still cuts a ton of weight at 145 so it does make you wonder. Choi did slow a bit to Nelson but I think there was ring rust there, his cardio held up pretty well against Algeo and that pace was similar to something Santos can set. I also think Willycat has a large hill to climb with the size; it;’s already an issue in prior fights but now he’s fighting someone who fights behind their range, with a diverse striking game and significantly more power. I do think Willycat can buzz and possibly even KO Choi, but I still think there is a sizable power discrepancy between the two. Willycat does have wrestling he can go to but im not sure how successful it will be. He uses it every fight but his control is not that good at 145; he weighs the same as most guys but his strength has not translated. He can get you down but Lee/Yoo stood up with little issue; even while tired Lee was still getting up. Choi can be taken down but he has really improved his grappling in this layoff. I think he can muscle his way to advantageous positions here, and if Willycat couldn’t hold Yoo/Lee down, I would be shocked if he can magically do it to a better grappler than both. I don’t expect Choi to be able to outgrapple Santos since he’s got really good bjj, but I wouldn’t be shocked if he can bully his way on top. If he can’t have success mixing in takedowns, I think this is an uphill battle for Santos. He can match the pace and can trade in the pocket with Choi but he is at a big physical disadvantage in many aspects, and I think Choi has a similar bag of tricks to him. Willycat has won a lot of his fights by taking a beating early and gassing his opponents out, but I didn’t like how his cardio looked in the Lee fight. This is a really hard one to call but I think Choi will craft it up again.

Wellmaker vs Diaz
Wellmaker KO RD 1
Trial by fire for Wellmaker; if he loses this one he’s in a really bad spot. I’ve personally never been high on Wellmaker and
still don’t, but I do think he wins this fight. Diaz has a flashy record but it’s padded with cans, while fun, the guy he beat on DWCS is not that good either. That was an all time KO he scored but I thought he lost r1 clearly and was slightly pulling ahead before the KO. Despite that elbow, Diaz is not very dangerous; that was his first KO in 5 years and I'm pretty sure the first time he’s ever put someone out cold. He is a striker but imo it’s not super impressive, he does fill the space well but I don’t think his boxing is that great; he doesn’t have a ton of power and he’s pretty hittable as well. I don’t think Wellmaker is a bad striker but I don’t like how he has his one signature shot and sticks to it. No shame in losing to Ewing but he got taken to school there, he had about 3 minutes of success and then got figured out. Wellmaker made Ewing work for it, and I don’t think he looked “bad” given the opponent, but that fight showed he still has a long way to go if he wants to live up to the hype. This also connects to the main reason I never liked Wellmaker in the first place, he is still too raw despite his age. I think he is solid but I worry he may be a finished product. That being said, I don’t think it’s super relevant here because I don’t rate Diaz. He is going to strike with Wellmaker and I don’t really think he excels in any one area. He does have better volume but not much power and I rhino his technique is bad; he loops his strikes a lot. Wellmaker is reliant on his hooks but he has a ton of power and great size/athleticism which helps. I think this is actually a really good matchup for him: Wellmaker is getting someone who is going to stand with him, isn’t an overly advanced striker, has no power, not a good athlete, and he’s hittable. Diaz does seem pretty durable but for all his flaws Wellmaker does hit extremely hard; that shot he hit Ewing with in r1 would’ve compromised a lot of people. I don’t think Wellmaker is some elite KO threat but if you are going to meet him in the pocket and strike, you are in for a long night. Diaz does have a high output but I don’t think he has the technical ability to avoid getting clipped at some point. I am still worried about Wellmaker’s ability to win outside of r1 but he did show good heart against Ewing and while down badly in r2/3, he still had some good moments; for example at the end of r2 he backed Ewing to the cage and stung him with a huge body shot, but Ewing perfectly timed a takedown to break up his rhythm. Diaz does occasionally shoot takedowns but I don’t think his wreslting is good at all. Wellmaker can be taken down but I think his get ups are good. Even in regional fights he showed he was hard to hold, and while a striker he got up instantly from Ewing’s shots. Wellmaker did get really tired around the halfway point but he didn’t quit on himself; I’m still not sure what to think of his cardio but I could definitely see a world where Diaz survives hell and can pace him. I’m not super confident because I don’t think Wellmaker is that good, but I think he should cruise against this level; Diaz has an impressive record and that vicious KO on dwcs, but he is largely unimpressive.

Bukauskas vs Bellato
Bellato KO RD 2

I’m not much of a Bellato guy but I like him in this spot. Both of these guys suck imo but I think Bellato is a really bad style for Modestas. Bellato is a zombie; he has no defense and a weirdly terrible chin, but he seemingly feels no pain and marches you down the entire fight. He nearly dies to everyone and has a glass jaw, yet he finds a way to not lose (most of the time). It’s always risky backing him because he’s such a liability, but I think this pressure heavy style is really bad for Modestas. Modestas is a point fighter who hates anything higher paced than a sparring match, and he somehow has an even worse chin than Bellato. Bellato at least recovers well, Modestas wobbles to the slightest touch and has been ko’ed 5 times; 4 of them out cold.I think his technical skills are great and he is definitely the better striker here, but Modestas needs to KO Bellato or else I fear he is going to get drowned. Modestas’s straight punches are money and he does have some power behind them, but at the UFC level he is just not a good KO threat. Besides having no KO’s over credible opposition, only one of them was from strikes at range; he was seconds from dragging Craig into r2 but got him with an elbow from top, and the Michalidis KO was Travis Browne elbows from a takedown. He does have power but at distance I don’t think he hits that hard. It’s also going to be hard for him to load up when he’s going to be the one going backwards the entire time. Bellato does get hurt in every fight yet somehow has managed to not get ko’ed in the UFC. Besides his chin, the fatal flaw of Modestas is that he has never learned how to protect himself in the pocket. Quite literally every fight of his he gets rocked or wobbled when exiting the pocket; this is because he leaves with his hands down and chin up in the air on every exchange. He’s never once picked up on this despite it nearly costing him multiple wins (Pauga, Prachnio, Ion - robbery). This worries me a ton in this matchup because Bellato isn’t going to give him space/room for a breather. He is going to walk him down and eat his best shots until he either gets ko’ed or ends the fight. Modestas has always struggled when the fight gets ugly and I really think he is going to get messed up against a zombie like this; you look at the Pauga/Prachnio fights and Modestas would look great at range, only to get hurt and fall apart the second they made the fight a little crazy. Bellato only knows craziness and while I usually hate backing him (especially against more technical fighters), it’s hard to not back him against a flake like Modestas. Not only is Bellato a bad style for him but I would argue Modestas is just as much of a liability to get slept, if not more; there is such a long track record of him getting hurt and falling apart when his opponents get too crazy. Modestas has improved since his first run but his wins are all against bums (besides the Ion robbery) and even then he still finds ways to struggle in most of them. He can definitely knock Bellato out because of how he fights, but imo Modestas either needs a round 1 KO or fight a perfect performance; and I just don’t think that’s going to be possible with how Bellato fights. Modestas cannot stay composed for 15 minutes without getting hurt or falling behind on volume, and we know Bellato is going to plod forward the entire fight until you sleep him.

Cuamba vs Sopaj
Sopaj KO RD 2

Really happy this fight is on the main card, I expect this to be a banger. I like both of these guys and the winner will probably get a big fight next. Both of these guys have their fair share of flaws but overall I think they are skilled. I like Cuamba at 135, he was clearly outmatched physically at 145. However, I’m not sure I like this matchup for him. He can have a lot of success but the way to beat Sopaj is you have to make him the nail. I don’t think his cardio is good but he’s clearly on EPO; he will look exhausted taking deep breaths, only to fire back with a multi-hit combo at 100% power. He looked like he was dead 2 minutes into the Turcios fight, only to beat him at his own game deep in r3. Turcios is a jobber but that fight was a good look to me; obviously it was ugly but it showed that on a full camp Sopaj can hold it together when things get tough. He also showed good heart, I didn’t like how he looked for the door against Lok Dog but he redeemed himself against Turcios. My problem with Cuamba in this fight is that he falls into the same trap as 75% of XC; he has all the skills but is content to cruise in fights. He doesn’t have a ton of power and struggles to separate a lot. I thought this would improve at 135 since he would be fighting people more his size (Lee also a former flyweight), yet he still dropped r1 with little resistance. He won r2 clearly but even then he didn’t really pull away until the last 2 minutes or so. I think he could potentially use this to his advantage because Sopaj does slow, but at the same time I haven’t really seen a fight where Cuamba just goes for it; he’s usually pretty measured and doesn’t like to get hit. Even his KO against Romero he was going through the motions until about 30 seconds prior to the flying knee. I think Cuamba has really good technical skills but I feel like he needs to match the craziness of Sopaj in order to come ahead. He will be able to land pretty easily but idk if he has the power to sway things. Sopaj hits really hard and he does a good job of always throwing with all his power; even if blocked it is a really good visual. I think this could especially be Cuamba’s downfall in this fight because he really struggles to separate in fights. His leg kicks are probably his best bet here, as it will slow down Sopaj over time and make his footwork more predictable. He really struggled with them against Lok Dog but I kind of think that had more to do with his power than an issue for Sopaj; he was throwing plenty of kicks himself and uses them quite frequently. I also think his passivity will allow Sopaj to dictate the pace and get it in close range where he wants. One thing that im still unsure of regarding Cuamba is his durability. I don’t think he’s chinny at all but imo he doesn’t like to get hit. You can see this with his overly cautious style but in his only loss he went diving for takedowns, got hit after some got stuffed, and just kind of wilted. That fight was a long time ago so maybe it’s not relevant, but we did see Cuamba get his head knocked around against Almeida as well. He doesn’t cut much weight but at 135 I am curious how he will deal with Sopaj’s power. Sopaj hits super hard and he also came very close to finishing both of his opponents in the UFC. He not only throws with everything but he has multiple one hit KO’s which you don’t see that often at 135. Cuamba does seem durable but I just have this feeling that he might wilt if Sopaj lands some flush combos on him. Both of these guys like to wrestle in their fights but I think it might cancel out. Both guys are hard to take down and Cuamba especially seems to struggle to get people down; he usually has to work you against the fence for a little. Sopaj is also pretty hard to take down due to his frame, and imo he has a very solid wrestling base. When taken down he is hard to hold, and he pops up quickly (while fresh), the same can’t be said for Cuamba. He is a really solid wrestler but when you put him on his back/in a dominant spot he really struggles to get up. He coasted all of r3 on his back in the Vogel fight, which ended up costing him a contract & nearly the fight. He also got stuck in the body triangle all of r1 against Lee. I don’t expect Sopaj to come in wrestle heavy but Cuamba has shown that he will mix it in in every fight. He can get takedowns but I don’t see him being able to control Sopaj for very long and if reversed/taken down, I think Sopaj can easily win minutes. He has shown really good top control and I personally have not liked what I’ve seen from Cuamba when put on his back. I never like long layoffs but Sopaj is still so young that I think it may be beneficial for him; you can always year so much with time off before your 30s. This is a close fight but I think Sopaj can keep the fight standing and do more than Cuamba. I’m on the fence between KO or DEC but I kind of have a feeling Sopaj can get him out of there.

Veretennikov vs Williams
Veretennikov DEC

This fight was a random last minute edition but I honestly love it; this is going to be a slobber knocker. I can understand why Khaos is the favorite here but it’s very hard for me to back him in 2026. I’ve never been a huge Khaos guy because he relies way too much on his athletic abilities to win fights. On a technical level, his striking is garbage; he does everything wrong in terms of setup, footwork, positioning, etc. He punches from his hips, loops every shot, leaves his chin on a platter, honestly his striking is amateur level, he just so happens to be athletic, powerful, and possessing a long reach. Khaos is also not a real fighter, he is a real estate agent who makes a yearly appearance every now and then. I don’t think he’s super dedicated to training and it has shown in recent performances. Even his last KO against Harris wasn’t that pretty; he ate a flush two piece on the jaw but Harris decided to trade in the pocket with him despite having no chin. His last performance was irredeemable, I don’t think Gustafsson is a good fighter and he beat the **** out of Khaos everywhere. The takedowns are somewhat irrelevant here since Nikolay doesn’t fight like that, but the fact Gustafsson was able to work him on the feet simply by crashing the space was a really bad look. Nikolay is also a weird fighter to back; he’s similar in some regards to Khaos in that he has a bad process and gets carried by his hardware. I think he’s got a much more complete game than Khaos but he fights like an ape; he just blindly walks you down with no defense. My main worry in backing Veretennikov is against wrestlers, but that is completely irrelevant here since Khaos has never even attempted a takedown in the ufc. In an all striking affair, I kind of like Veretennikov here. He’s very hittable and will fight the fight that Khaos wants, but I also think he’s got better technique and Khaos has overrated power. Nikolay could get bonked but he’s actually really durable, and Khaos a terrible striker. He does hit hard but he isn’t knocking everyone out because he has absolutely no clue how to throw punches properly. He just flails his arms around and hopes something lands. He will be able to land a lot, but I also think Nikolay can stand & trade with him, without worrying about dying in evcery exchange; it is live to happen with how these two fight, but I kind of think Khaos’s gimmick has run its course. Nikolay’s striking is basic but not bad at all, I think he can outwork Khaos with his jab and leg kicks. I can also see Nikolay clinching here; he does a really good job with his knees in the clinch, and it takes away a lot of Khaos’s danger. Khaos has fought enough guys with terrible striking defense at this point (Bedoya, Gustafsson) that I think I can trust Nikolay enough to not get slept; he has survived some brutal strikes and his only recent ko loss was gnp. In an all striking match its going to be close and very ugly, but I kind of like Veretennikov here. He won’t be afraid of Khaos and is the better striker here. Khaos has a prettier record but he is a big time overachiever and recently does not seem to care that much about fighting. Khaos is also entirely reliant on his physical traits as a crutch, where Veretennikov has good hardware and better technique. This is going to be an ugly bar brawl but I will take Nikolay at any dog money; Khaos is KO or bust here imo

Allen vs. Costa
Arnold Allen, DEC
I think we get a master class from Arnold Allen here. He’s been on the wrong side of some competitive decisions lately but they were against elite guys at the top of the division. Melky had arguably the best 2025 of any featherweight but he’s a bit of an overachiever imo considering his win streak has some pretty mid names on that list but some impressive KOs against durable guys in his last two which does give him some well deserved credit. I think Melky is good enough to be in ranked I just think he is shown levels here. Allen has a lot more physicality and athleticism than Melky’s previous opponents and I think that presents a lot more challenges especially over 5 rounds. I’m saying Arnold wins here by either decision or TKO.

Choi vs. Santos
Daniel Santos, TKO, R2
This feels like an easy pick here. Choi had a good performance against a washed Nate the Train but when you look at his resume he’s never really beaten anyone note worthy. He’s got that label of a guy who will “go to war” but if you’re doing that and losing or doing that against low level guys, I don’t really look at you as this crafty vet capable of pulling a big upset. Santos is too well rounded and I think he’s honestly the much more dangerous guy on the feet even with the size disadvantage. I think he finishes Choi by either KO or Sub.

Wellmaker vs. Díaz
Malcolm Wellmaker, DEC
For all my degenerate gamblers this is what we call a “buy low spot” for Wellmaker. Sure he lost as a huge favorite his last fight but I don’t think anyone would have predicted Ethyn Ewing to be one of the best boxers in the division before even making his debut. So you almost have to go back and reevaluate Wellmakers last performance with a grain of salt and when you think about it it was a pretty close 29-28 decision against a high level guy on short notice. That is the type of loss I think he grows from and I think we see him level up a bit here. I’m gonna say he wins by decision because these Peruvian dudes all seem to be tough as nails with good chins, but Wellmaker is for sure the pick here.

Bukauskas vs. Bellato
Rodolfo Bellato, TKO, R2
Time to wake up folks, Bukauskas is overrated. I know he’s had some good performances against some bums but he consistently underperforms when you give him a step up in competition. Bellato might not be the smartest or most skilled guy but he’s not a bottom of the barrel guy who Modestas can just pick away at range against. Bellato is a force that’s constantly moving forward, eating shots, and throwing heavy bombs. I could see him having some issues with the leg kicks of Modestas early but honestly it’s only a matter of time till he gasses out and lowers the hands a bit when he’s carrying around all that muscle and Bellato fights at such a high pace. I think we see a round 2-3 KO by Bellato and a bunch of parlays get ruined.

Can't believe I'm saying this, but I think I'm going to switch up and pick Cody Brundage to win a fight. Big Brundage. Blonde Brundage. The GOAT Brundage. I've been thinking about this fight a LOT: WAY more than anyone should ever think about a Cody Brundage fight. Here's the thing, you guys: Brundage has had decent moments in most of his recent fights. He arguably won the Donte Johnson and Eric McConico fights, and in the McConico, Rowston, and Abdul-Malik fights, he managed to find the chin and give his opponents some trouble with his striking, even if it wasn't enough to win because Brundage is maybe the least reliable guy in the promotion and always looks for an easy way out. The factor that I keep coming back to in this fight, though, is that Andre Petroski has one of the worst chins in the UFC. He knocked himself out shooting a takedown by colliding with Jacob Malkoun's hipbone, and that check hook from Cam Rowston that dropped Petroski one fight ago didn't look too powerful. Brundage might not be a power puncher, but again, he rocked Rowston and McConico. If you can rock Rowston and McConico, I think you can put out Andre Petroski. Petroski, in comparison, has very little finishing upside, so his gameplan here has to be to get about 10 minutes of control time and win a terrible decision or get a submission after Brundage enters the second half of R2 and decides to give up. To my knowledge, Brundage has only been submitted in the UFC by guys with pretty decent grappling like Robert Nickal and Rodolfo Vieira. Petroski is probably the better wrestler between these two, but he hasn't been looking great recently even when we're talking about the strongest aspect of his game. Cam Rowston's goofy, slow-paced striking and his history of getting smudged by guys like Torrez Finney ought to have made him a good matchup for Petroski, but Petroski didn't even shoot a takedown in that fight. He secured less than half a minute of control time on Edmen Shahbazyan. Now, I like Edmen as a fighter, and yes, he's probably been working a lot on his TDD after that horrible fumble against GM3, and yes, Edmen fought at kicking range that whole fight to nullify the takedown threat from Petroski as much as possible, but historically speaking, pretty much anyone who has wanted to take down Edmen Shahbazyan in the UFC has been able to do so. To me, that is a strong sign that Petroski is losing or has lost the ability to get opponents to the mat and keep them there. The last three guys that Petroski was able to hold down and smudge to a decision win were Josh Fremd, Dylan Budka, and Wellington Turman. I realize I am talking about Big Brundage here, the guy who has been out there looking downright terrible, but I think he has better grappling than Budka, Fremd, or Turman. I recognize that we saw Boonk Gang show Brundage levels in the wrestling, but that was back in 2023, and Brundage has shown better wrestling in his fights since then, although I recognize that's not saying much. Say what you want about the strength of schedule, but Brundage's last few fights have at least been against genuinely athletic guys, and for whatever reason, Petroski has been moving in the octagon like he's ancient even though he's only 34. He just seems sapped of his speed and athleticism, and even though Brundage is prone to gassing and quitting, he has at least shown athletic rounds recently. I think Petroski is really going to struggle to get Brundage down and keep him down, and when they're on the feet, I think all Brundage needs to do is get a good bonk in to win the fight. Oh, and a couple of intangibles to consider. If Brundage loses this fight, he HAS to be cut, right? He must know that, and one would imagine that this motivation to stay in the UFC would counteract Brundage's tendency to do the Anthony Smith turtle-in-his-shell routine. Plus, I believe that the UFC likes Brundage. He's bottom-rung, so they probably aren't paying him much money, and he shows up every time they need somebody to take a short notice fight. He's getting a fight here that isn't on short notice, for once, and I think it's possible that the UFC is setting him up for a win here so that they can hang onto him for a few more short notice matchups.

Arnold Allen by unanimous decision
This is a nasty main event because Costa is not some random guy getting a bump — he is dangerous, confident, and he is coming in with real momentum. But Allen is the more layered fighter. He can box southpaw, stay defensively responsible, calf kick, clinch, reset, and win minutes without needing chaos. Costa’s path is pressure, body work, and forcing Allen into exchanges where the fight becomes less technical and more attritional. The issue is Allen is usually very composed in that exact kind of fight. Over five rounds, I trust Allen’s discipline, counters, and strength of schedule more.

Daniel Santos by TKO, Round 2
This has violence written all over it. Choi is still one of those guys where, when he gets his boxing rhythm, he can crack you with clean, beautiful straight shots and hooks in combination. But Santos brings a more modern chaos game: pressure, spinning attacks, pace, knees, and he is going to make Choi fight at a speed where defensive reactions matter every second. Choi’s boxing is cleaner, but Santos is more likely to turn it into a storm. I think he hurts Choi in transition and swarms.

Malcolm Wellmaker by TKO, Round 1
Wellmaker feels like the pick because he has the cleaner upside and more dangerous finishing gear. Díaz has to survive early, make this ugly, and test whether Wellmaker can stay composed when the first-layer offense does not immediately work. But Wellmaker is explosive, sharp, and I think he is going to find the timing before Díaz can settle into the fight. This is one where the first round matters a lot.

Modestas Bukauskas by TKO, Round 2
This one changed late, and that matters. Edwards is athletic, long, and dangerous enough that you cannot just write him off, especially because short-notice debut guys sometimes fight with zero fear. But Bukauskas is the more seasoned UFC-level fighter, and he has been through much tougher looks. I think he pressures Edwards backward, kicks the body and legs, and eventually punishes him once Edwards starts reacting instead of initiating. Edwards’ best shot is a fast start and an explosive counter, but Bukauskas should be the more reliable minute-winner.

Bernardo Sopaj by submission, Round 2
Sopaj is the more dangerous all-around finisher. Cuamba can absolutely make this competitive if he keeps it long, stays disciplined, and forces Sopaj to work through clean entries. But Sopaj has that grappling threat that changes the way the striking exchanges happen. Once Cuamba starts worrying about takedowns and clinch pressure, the openings get bigger. I like Sopaj to get to the back or force a scramble and find the neck.

Khaos Williams by TKO, Round 1
This is the fight where you can almost hear the impact before it happens. Veretennikov is tough and dangerous, but Khaos Williams has terrifying first-round power. He does not need a long combination; he needs one clean read, one overhand, one counter, and suddenly the whole fight changes. Veretennikov’s path is to extend the fight, clinch, make Khaos work, and drag him past that initial explosion. I just think Khaos lands something huge before that happens.

@Nietzsche I think the odds are okay. I've been in a situation numerous times recently with fighters that have long standing, serious health issues and I always tell myself I'll never pick them because of it, but it hasn't actually mattered - until they lose, which is how this always goes. Recent examples -

Tatiana Suarez - Cancer + Thyroid (?), Loses clearly to Zhang, then wins clearly in her next two fights. Health history and problems unchanged.

Khamzat Chimaev - Auto Immune disorder + Thyroid (?) - Known since before Whittaker fight. Defeats Whittaker and DDP without issue, then loses and looks fatigued early.

Maycee Barber - Has nervous system problems and seizures, calls off a fight with Blanchfield, then comes back with these same health issues and wins a fight without any health problems, seemingly. Then in her next fight, it's easy to argue her health issues contributed to her KO (Regardless of whether or not she was cleared to fight despite them).

So all I'm saying is that in the above three examples, if you said "BRO THEY GOT A SERIOUS HEALTH PROBLEM THEY GOT NO CHANCE" You'd have been wrong several times a piece. Additionally, all three examples are at the top of their respective divisions. Also, all three of those fighters had breaks where their health issues were bad, then they came back. Milky has just been fighting this whole time regardless, plus he has the money now for relevant treatments.

Not saying his personal health issues should be ignored, but I don't think they matter that much actually, and I've personally been trying to really lean on chronic/longstanding health issues for picks and it just hasn't flown at all, if I am being honest.

Allen Vs Costa
Allen TKO R4
After reviewing tape I have come to a slightly different conclusion than I had before I started properly deliberating, albeit I am more informed now. Costa is still the more dangerous fighter overall in this matchup, I can see the rear head kick posing a great danger due to this being a closed stance matchup ultimately however I don't think Costa does have the pressure, or the pace to create a KO here, which is what I see his primary path to victory being. Melquizael generally finds his KO's at range, as in he finds a KO when his opponent attempts to close distance. Examples:   Ige: Costa capitilized on Ige's habit of bracing and dipping low when intercepted with a strike as he attempts to close into boxing range- hard to tell with cam angle not showing legs but it'd seem Costa is either feinting a low kick or spinning backfist by posture.Charriere: At range as Charriere is circling off, Costa throws his rear high kick but doesn't turn his hips until he's almost halfway through the motion. This makes the kick appear much more like a rear teep to the gut, you can see this is what Charriere expects as he attempts to parry around that area with the lead hand. Costa's setup is also more obvious from the fact that he fell immediately after the kick, having to hit a retreating target whilst also delaying the motion of the hips threw him off balance. Melo (LFA Title): Looks different than his other KO's because it is at boxing range and is done with an overhand, but still he pulls into range rather than closing range. As Melo attempts to close distance Costa intercepts Melo's straight with his lead hand, then uses that same hand as a post to throw his body momentum into the left overhand- as Melo moves into it. Knocking Melo down and leading to a GNP TKO.Buzika/Ferreira (SFT): Quite different from the other KO's, as this one is more chaotic and the finishing sequence ends with Costa dropping Ferreira with a leaping left hook. But the finishing sequence itself starts when Ferreira hesitates throwing his teep as Costa parries with the rear hand- he then lands forward awkardly and bent over his hips- leading to him being caught with Costa's left overhand around his arm, landing behind the ear- afterward he is also immediately caught with another left hook across the cheek. Costa's striking is rather unique overall, he fights properly taekwondo-esque- rather than Muay Thai like for someone out of ChuteBoxe. At moments you can see in his fights he blades almost completely and bounces on the balls of his feet, an instinct you can immediately recognize from point Taekwondo competitions. In that way it explains his dynamic kicking game, and the additional fact that his pure boxing technique is rather poor on its' own. His punches largely either come from the hips or the waist, and he winds and puts his bodily momentum into most ones, even his jab. Though this does not mean his punches are entirely ineffective, as mentioned before he can still KO and damage with them, mostly by the fact that he swings wide and with the momentum of his body, he sort of runs or leaps into his punches when advancing. His fast-twitch/explosivity is not deniable however, and the punches can still serve damage his opponent or to keep their  pressure from resulting in damage, also setting up step in knees, or moves into the clinch (Where he can work additional knees or work to the ground, or slow opponent's momentum and pressure and then break contact and move to range). Costa prefers to fight on the backfoot at mid range, often his back as at the fence (He tends to throw a superman punch from this position, mostly to create distance if opponent is in boxing range)- working into his game of attacking an opponent attempting to close into boxing distance with him, this is where the majority of his KO threat arises, as shown earlier. Whether Costa is advancing, retreating, or neutral at range he mostly prefers to throw the rear leg rather than the lead (Lead leg is usually used only for outside calf kicks and obliques or thigh stomps in open stance, he does not teep with lead), even kicking from the same side immediately after the other (Example is R1 Vs Erosa, first strikes by Costa are lead calf kick, rear calf kick, read body kick, rear teep, all within first 40 seconds). Moving on, Allen is a fair bit less unique than Costa, and I tend to think he's quite simple overall. This does mean he can be a lot more practical at most times though, and is more of a jack of all trades in MMA rather than a specialist like Costa. While I have outlined how Costa has gotten KO's, and I did believe he would get KO'd in this fight (Which is Costa's primary means of victory in my opinion, I do not think he has the cardio to go five rounds for a decision), upon my further analysis I don't think Allen will be finished anymore. For one, he adapts his defensive tactics to each opponent he faces, I attribute this mostly to the fact that he is coached by Fares Zahabi, one of the best minds in MMA. Examples are thus:  Low and loose probing lead hand with rear glued to the chin against Evloev, in order to feel out range and prevent Evloev from pressuring in and forcing him to the fence where he can work to get single legs or double legs against the cage much more easily, meaning Evloev has to shoot more obviously in the open and work for longer on the feet with him, also can be used to dig to quickly dig an underhook and sprawl. Tight, sort of, Kyokushin guard with arms squared by the body and chin crunched inward to chest when fighting Holloway to lean into strikes, the high guard for punches- elbows and forearms for kicks, with lateral movement Max's punches around the guard weren't as much of an issue as he could no longer as easily set up his boxing combinations and tee off on a stationary or open target (I think Allen will use a similar stance to this, maybe with the lead leg turned slightly more outward and lead arm lower on the ribs, at least that's what I believe Fares Zahabi should advise Allen to do).   In addition Allen normally has his rear leg wide and nearly straight behind his lead- mostly so he can leap off of the lead and out of range, but this is also the source of his bad defensive habit: Tending to retreat linearly whilst leaning on the rear leg, in response to combinations or spinning strikes, leaving him susceptible to pressure. There was also a moment where Allen was dropped by Evloev when closing distance, which would lead me to believe him to be more likely of being finished by Costa if not for the specific circumstances of the knockdown. It happened as both fighters closed distance to land their jabs, Evloev essentially beat Allen to the punch while planting and having Allen moving into his strike, but I do believe Allen only was caught this badly because he had his lead hand so low and far out from the guard so he could dig an underhook and maintain range on Evloev's takedown attempts (Also it was a very, very, brief knockdown where Allen maintained momentum and bodily tension through it, making it unviable for a finish)- essentially I'm saying this only happened because Allen was fighting in a very specific way in an attempt to counter Evloev, who found a hole his technique by timing a jab entry. Anyway, I think Allen's stance and guard will make it so he can both move out of the range of Costa's more dangerous strikes consistently as well as guard/absorb fairly well (Moreso high kicks, it did happen repeatedly that Max was able to tag Allen with roundhouses to the body and kicks to the calf more often than Allen defended those strikes), neutralizing much of Costa's offence. Which is primarily made up of kicks currently, Costa can use all of them to score well and set up more impactful strikes- especially the rear calf kick will be useful with Allen's more bladed stance. This is why I see the striking as being fairly competitive between these two, Allen having the edge in a few areas (Overall boxing, shot absorption/guard defense, cardio, offensive+defensive footwork), Costa others (Range management, shot selection/accuracy, large strike setups/counters, kicking game). I've explained why I don't think Costa will get a finish but for Allen whilst I don't have much faith in his KO power or aggression Costa has tired out horrendously against Erosa and Rodriguez in the 3rd rounds of both fights, his boxing defense also looked fairly atrocious when he does gas out (and even before he does gas out his boxing defense is fairly poor, it is more often that he gets tagged on the chin than anywhere else) and I think if or when the fight reaches that point it's likely Allen will pour on volume and find a finish. It's not often that Allen does put his foot on the gas, but we've seen he's capable of pursuing a finish when he needs to or the opportunity arises, like R3 Vs Evloev, or immediately against Hooker (it's just that Allen doesn't force a finish the majority of the time). For the likelihood of this fight going to the ground where Costa could work his BJJ and get a sub is minimal due neither of the guys having particularly distinctive skills in offensive wrestling. I say offensive wrestling/grappling because of the fact that Evloev was not able to control Allen, so I do value his defensive skills in that area quite highly, which makes strengthens my belief that I see the vast, vast, majority of the fight taking place on the feet. Maybe (?) unless Costa jumps on a guillotine or ninja choke from by getting a thai clinch like the one he briefly useg against Ige (still fairly unlikely in my opinion, Allen would need to be quite static- which does not describe him). I don't think it's completely impossible that with damage Costa can force a more low output mid-range battle which he can sc**** a win by decision, or even get a KO off of Allen for that matter (If he sets up well and is able to find a way to get Allen to move into range and lower his guard), but I ultimately see it as less likely than the afformentioned scenario of Allen by late round 4 TKO- which is why I'm picking that.

This does happen Greasy WMMA Opener vibes to it tho so I’ll take Shauna to get her hand raise after some suspense.

Luis Gurule via Decision
I don’t like this little person fight, I don’t trust either of these two. I have a hunch Gurule has thrown fights in the past (It’s time to throw away all your journalistic credibility and get reckless, this is something we call Reckless Speculation) and it’s just tough to take him seriously. Barez is old for a Flyweight, isn’t very active to begin with and isn’t going to make a run anytime soon. If Gurule can’t win this, cut his ass.
